1.mohsin_khan: Ha-Mim. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Quran and none but Allah (Alone) knows their meanings].

2.pickthall: By the Scripture that maketh plain
2.yusuf_ali: By the Book that makes things clear;-
2.shakir: I swear by the Book that makes manifest (the truth).
2.muhammad_sarwar: I swear by the illustrious Book.
2.mohsin_khan: By the manifest Book (this Quran) that makes things clear,

3.sahih_international: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn [mankind].
3.pickthall: Lo! We revealed it on a blessed night - Lo! We are ever warning -
3.yusuf_ali: We sent it down during a Blessed Night: for We (ever) wish to warn (against Evil).
3.shakir: Surely We revealed it on a blessed night surely We are ever warning--
3.muhammad_sarwar: that We have revealed the Quran on a blessed night to warn mankind.
3.mohsin_khan: We sent it (this Quran) down on a blessed night [(i.e. night of Qadr, Surah No: 97) in the month of Ramadan,, the 9th month of the Islamic calendar]. Verily, We are ever warning [mankind that Our Torment will reach those who disbelieve in Our Oneness of Lordship and in Our Oneness of worship].
3.arberry: We have sent it down in a blessed night (We are ever warning)

4.sahih_international: On that night is made distinct every precise matter -
4.pickthall: Whereon every wise command is made clear
4.yusuf_ali: In the (Night) is made distinct every affair of wisdom,
4.shakir: Therein every wise affair is made distinct,
4.muhammad_sarwar: On this night, every absolute command coming from Us becomes distinguishable.
4.mohsin_khan: Therein (that night) is decreed every matter of ordainments.

5.sahih_international: [Every] matter [proceeding] from Us. Indeed, We were to send [a messenger]
5.pickthall: As a command from Our presence - Lo! We are ever sending -
5.yusuf_ali: By command, from Our Presence. For We (ever) send (revelations),
5.shakir: A command from Us; surely We are the senders (of apostles),
5.muhammad_sarwar: The command that We have been sending
5.mohsin_khan: Amran (i.e. a Command or this Quran or the Decree of every matter) from Us. Verily, We are ever sending (the Messengers),
5.arberry: determined as a bidding from Us, (We are ever sending)

6.sahih_international: As mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
6.pickthall: A mercy from thy Lord. Lo! He, even He is the Hearer, the Knower,
6.yusuf_ali: As Mercy from thy Lord: for He hears and knows (all things);
6.shakir: A mercy from your Lord, surely He is the Hearing, the Knowing,
6.muhammad_sarwar: as a mercy (for the human being) from your Lord. Your Lord is All-hearing and All-knowing.
6.mohsin_khan: (As) a Mercy from your Lord. Verily! He is the All-Hearer, the All-Knower.
6.arberry: as a mercy from thy Lord (surely He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing)

7.sahih_international: Lord of the heavens and the earth and that between them, if you would be certain.
7.pickthall: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if ye would be sure.
7.yusuf_ali: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all between them, if ye (but) have an assured faith.
7.shakir: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if you would be sure.
7.muhammad_sarwar: He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if only you would have strong faith.
7.mohsin_khan: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if you (but) have a faith with certainty.
7.arberry: Lord of the heavens and earth, and all that between them is if you have faith.

8.sahih_international: There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. [He is] your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.
8.pickthall: There is no Allah save Him. He quickeneth and giveth death; your Lord and Lord of your forefathers.
8.yusuf_ali: There is no god but He: It is He Who gives life and gives death,- The Lord and Cherisher to you and your earliest ancestors.
8.shakir: There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your fathers of yore.
8.muhammad_sarwar: There is only One Lord. It is He who gives life and causes things to die. He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.
8.mohsin_khan: La ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He). It is He Who gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your fore-fathers.
8.arberry: There is no god but He; He gives life and makes to die; your Lord and the Lord of your fathers, the ancients.

9.sahih_international: But they are in doubt, amusing themselves.
9.pickthall: Nay, but they play in doubt.
9.yusuf_ali: Yet they play about in doubt.
9.shakir: Nay, they are in doubt, they sport.
9.muhammad_sarwar: In fact, the unbelievers have doubts because of excessive involvement in worldly affairs.
9.arberry: Nay, but they are in doubt, playing.

10.sahih_international: Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke.
10.pickthall: But watch thou (O Muhammad) for the day when the sky will produce visible smoke
10.yusuf_ali: Then watch thou for the Day that the sky will bring forth a kind of smoke (or mist) plainly visible,
10.shakir: Therefore keep waiting for the day when the heaven shall bring an evident smoke,
10.muhammad_sarwar: Wait for the day (which will come before the Day of Judgment) when the sky will give out dense smoke
10.mohsin_khan: Then wait you for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke.
10.arberry: So be on the watch for a day when heaven shall bring a manifest smoke

11.sahih_international: Covering the people; this is a painful torment.
11.pickthall: That will envelop the people. This will be a painful torment.
11.yusuf_ali: Enveloping the people: this will be a Penalty Grievous.
11.shakir: That shall overtake men; this is a painful punishment.
11.muhammad_sarwar: which will smother the people. They will say, "This is a painful torment.
11.mohsin_khan: Covering the people, this is a painful torment.
11.arberry: covering the people; this is a painful chastisement.

12.sahih_international: [They will say], "Our Lord, remove from us the torment; indeed, we are believers."
12.pickthall: (Then they will say): Our Lord relieve us of the torment. Lo! we are believers.
12.yusuf_ali: (They will say:) "Our Lord! remove the Penalty from us, for we do really believe!"
12.shakir: Our Lord! remove from us the punishment; surely we are believers.
12.muhammad_sarwar: Lord, remove this torment from us for we are believers".
12.mohsin_khan: (They will say): "Our Lord! Remove the torment from us, really we shall become believers!"
12.arberry: 'O our Lord, remove Thou from us the chastisement; we are believers.'

13.sahih_international: How will there be for them a reminder [at that time]? And there had come to them a clear Messenger.
13.pickthall: How can there be remembrance for them, when a messenger making plain (the Truth) had already come unto them,
13.yusuf_ali: How shall the message be (effectual) for them, seeing that an Messenger explaining things clearly has (already) come to them,-
13.shakir: How shall they be reminded, and there came to them an Apostle making clear (the truth),
13.muhammad_sarwar: How could this punishment bring them to their senses when a Messenger evidently had come to them,
13.mohsin_khan: How can there be for them an admonition (at the time when the torment has reached them), when a Messenger explaining things clearly has already come to them.
13.arberry: How should they have the Reminder, seeing a clear Messenger already came to them,

14.sahih_international: Then they turned away from him and said, "[He was] taught [and is] a madman."
14.pickthall: And they had turned away from him and said: One taught (by others), a madman?
14.yusuf_ali: Yet they turn away from him and say: "Tutored (by others), a man possessed!"
14.shakir: Yet they turned their backs on him and said: One taught (by others), a madman.
14.muhammad_sarwar: and they turned away, saying, "He is a trained and insane person".
14.mohsin_khan: Then they had turned away from him (Messenger Muhammad SAW) and said: "One (Muhammad SAW) taught (by a human being), a madman!"
14.arberry: then they turned away from him and said, 'A man tutored, possessed!'

15.sahih_international: Indeed, We will remove the torment for a little. Indeed, you [disbelievers] will return [to disbelief].
15.pickthall: Lo! We withdraw the torment a little. Lo! ye return (to disbelief).
15.yusuf_ali: We shall indeed remove the Penalty for a while, (but) truly ye will revert (to your ways).
15.shakir: Surely We will remove the punishment a little, (but) you will surely return (to evil).
15.muhammad_sarwar: We shall remove the torment for a while but you will revert to your old ways.
15.mohsin_khan: Verily, We shall remove the torment for a while. Verily! You will revert.
15.arberry: 'Behold, We are removing the chastisement a little; behold, you revert!'

16.sahih_international: The Day We will strike with the greatest assault, indeed, We will take retribution.
16.pickthall: On the day when We shall seize them with the greater seizure, (then) in truth We shall punish.
16.yusuf_ali: One day We shall seize you with a mighty onslaught: We will indeed (then) exact Retribution!
16.shakir: On the day when We will seize (them) with the most violent seizing; surely We will inflict retribution.
16.muhammad_sarwar: However, We shall truly take Our revenge on the day when the great seizure takes place.
16.mohsin_khan: On the Day when We shall seize you with the greatest grasp. Verily, We will exact retribution.
16.arberry: Upon the day when We shall assault most mightily, then We shall take Our vengeance.

17.sahih_international: And We had already tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger,
17.pickthall: And verily We tried before them Pharaoh's folk, when there came unto them a noble messenger,
17.yusuf_ali: We did, before them, try the people of Pharaoh: there came to them a messenger most honourable,
17.shakir: And certainly We tried before them the people of Firon, and there came to them a noble apostle,
17.muhammad_sarwar: We had certainly tested the people of the Pharaoh before them to whom a noble Messengers had come, saying,
17.mohsin_khan: And indeed We tried before them Fir'aun's (Pharaoh) people, when there came to them a noble Messenger [i.e. Musa (Moses)],
17.arberry: Already before them We tried the people of Pharaoh, and a noble Messenger came unto them,

18.sahih_international: [Saying], "Render to me the servants of Allah. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger,"
18.pickthall: Saying: Give up to me the slaves of Allah. Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you.
18.yusuf_ali: Saying: "Restore to me the Servants of Allah: I am to you an messenger worthy of all trust;
18.shakir: Saying: Deliver to me the servants of Allah, surely I am a faithful apostle to you,
18.muhammad_sarwar: "Send the servants of God with me. I am a trustworthy Messenger sent to you.
18.mohsin_khan: Saying: "Restore to me the slaves of Allah (i.e. the Children of Israel). Verily! I am to you a Messenger worthy of all trust,
18.arberry: saying, 'Deliver to me God's servants; I am for you a faithful Messenger,

19.sahih_international: And [saying], "Be not haughty with Allah. Indeed, I have come to you with clear authority.
19.pickthall: And saying: Be not proud against Allah. Lo! I bring you a clear warrant.
19.yusuf_ali: "And be not arrogant as against Allah: for I come to you with authority manifest.
19.shakir: And that do not exalt yourselves against Allah, surely I will bring to you a clear authority:
19.muhammad_sarwar: Do not consider yourselves above God? I shall show you a manifest authority (in support of my truthfulness).
19.mohsin_khan: "And exalt not (yourselves) against Allah. Truly, I have come to you with a manifest authority.
19.arberry: and, 'Rise not up against God; behold, I come to you with a clear authority,

20.sahih_international: And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.
20.pickthall: And lo! I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest ye stone me to death.
20.yusuf_ali: "For me, I have sought safety with my Lord and your Lord, against your injuring me.
20.shakir: And surely I take refuge with my Lord and your Lord that you should stone me to death:
20.muhammad_sarwar: I seek protection from my Lord and your Lord from your decision of stoning me.
20.mohsin_khan: "And truly, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me (or call me a sorcerer or kill me).
20.arberry: and I take refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you should stone me.

21.sahih_international: But if you do not believe me, then leave me alone."
21.pickthall: And if ye put no faith in me, then let me go.
21.yusuf_ali: "If ye believe me not, at least keep yourselves away from me."
21.shakir: And if you do not believe in me, then leave me alone.
21.muhammad_sarwar: If you do not want to believe, leave me alone".
21.mohsin_khan: "But if you believe me not, then keep away from me and leave me alone."
21.arberry: 'But if so be that you believe me not, go you apart from me!'

22.sahih_international: And [finally] he called to his Lord that these were a criminal people.
22.pickthall: And he cried unto his Lord, (saying): These are guilty folk.
22.yusuf_ali: (But they were aggressive:) then he cried to his Lord: "These are indeed a people given to sin."
22.shakir: Then he called upon his Lord: These are a guilty people.
22.muhammad_sarwar: Moses addressed his Lord, saying, "Lord, these people are sinners".
22.mohsin_khan: (But they were aggressive), so he [Musa (Moses)] called upon his Lord (saying): "These are indeed the people who are Mujrimun (disbelievers, polytheists, sinners, criminals, etc.)."
22.arberry: And he called to his Lord, saying, 'These are a sinful people.'

23.sahih_international: [Allah said], "Then set out with My servants by night. Indeed, you are to be pursued.
23.pickthall: Then (his Lord commanded): Take away My slaves by night. Lo! ye will be followed,
23.yusuf_ali: (The reply came:) "March forth with My Servants by night: for ye are sure to be pursued.
23.shakir: So go forth with My servants by night; surely you will be pursued:
23.muhammad_sarwar: We told him, "Leave the city with My servants during the night. You will be pursued.
23.mohsin_khan: (Allah said): "Depart you with My slaves by night. Surely, you will be pursued.
23.arberry: 'Then set thou forth with My servants in a watch of the night; surely you will be followed.

24.sahih_international: And leave the sea in stillness. Indeed, they are an army to be drowned."
24.pickthall: And leave the sea behind at rest, for lo! they are a drowned host.
24.yusuf_ali: "And leave the sea as a furrow (divided): for they are a host (destined) to be drowned."
24.shakir: And leave the sea intervening; surely they are a host that shall be drowned.
24.muhammad_sarwar: Cross the sea by cutting a path through it. Pharaoh's army will be drowned.
24.mohsin_khan: "And leave the sea as it is (quiet and divided). Verily, They are a host to be drowned."
24.arberry: And leave the sea becalmed; they are a drowned host.'

25.sahih_international: How much they left behind of gardens and springs
25.pickthall: How many were the gardens and the watersprings that they left behind,
25.yusuf_ali: How many were the gardens and springs they left behind,
25.shakir: How many of the gardens and fountains have they left!
25.muhammad_sarwar: How many were the gardens, springs,
25.mohsin_khan: How many of gardens and springs do they [Fir'aun's (Pharaoh) people] left.
25.arberry: They left how many gardens and fountains,

26.pickthall: And the cornlands and the goodly sites
26.mohsin_khan: And green crops (fields etc.) and goodly places,
26.arberry: sown fields, and how noble a station,

27.sahih_international: And comfort wherein they were amused.
27.pickthall: And pleasant things wherein they took delight!
27.yusuf_ali: And wealth (and conveniences of life), wherein they had taken such delight!
27.shakir: And goodly things wherein they rejoiced;
27.muhammad_sarwar: and other bounties which they enjoyed yet left behind!
27.mohsin_khan: And comforts of life wherein they used to take delight!
27.arberry: and what prosperity they had rejoiced in!

28.sahih_international: Thus. And We caused to inherit it another people.
28.pickthall: Even so (it was), and We made it an inheritance for other folk;
28.yusuf_ali: Thus (was their end)! And We made other people inherit (those things)!
28.shakir: Thus (it was), and We gave them as a heritage to another people.
28.muhammad_sarwar: We gave these as an inheritance to other people.
28.mohsin_khan: Thus (it was)! And We made other people inherit them (i.e. We made the Children of Israel to inherit the kingdom of Egypt).
28.arberry: Even so; and We bequeathed them upon another people.

29.sahih_international: And the heaven and earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved.
29.pickthall: And the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved.
29.yusuf_ali: And neither heaven nor earth shed a tear over them: nor were they given a respite (again).
29.shakir: So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they respited.
29.muhammad_sarwar: The sky nor the earth cried for them, nor were they given respite.
29.mohsin_khan: And the heavens and the earth wept not for them, nor were they given a respite.
29.arberry: Neither heaven nor earth wept for them, nor were they respited;

30.sahih_international: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment -
30.pickthall: And We delivered the Children of Israel from the shameful doom;
30.yusuf_ali: We did deliver aforetime the Children of Israel from humiliating Punishment,
30.shakir: And certainly We delivered the children of Israel from the abasing chastisement,
30.muhammad_sarwar: We rescued the Israelites from the humiliating torment
30.mohsin_khan: And indeed We saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment,
30.arberry: and We delivered the Children of Israel from the humbling chastisement,

31.sahih_international: From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was a haughty one among the transgressors.
31.pickthall: (We delivered them) from Pharaoh. Lo! he was a tyrant of the wanton ones.
31.yusuf_ali: Inflicted by Pharaoh, for he was arrogant (even) among inordinate transgressors.
31.shakir: From Firon; surely he was haughty, (and) one of the extravagant.
31.muhammad_sarwar: and from the Pharaoh. He was the chief of the transgressors.
31.mohsin_khan: From Fir'aun (Pharaoh); Verily! He was arrogant and was of the Musrifun (those who transgress beyond bound in spending and other things and commit great sins).
31.arberry: from Pharaoh; surely he was a high One, of the prodigals;

32.sahih_international: And We certainly chose them by knowledge over [all] the worlds.
32.pickthall: And We chose them, purposely, above (all) creatures.
32.yusuf_ali: And We chose them aforetime above the nations, knowingly,
32.shakir: And certainly We chose them, having knowledge, above the nations.
32.muhammad_sarwar: We gave preference to the Israelites over the other people with Our knowledge
32.mohsin_khan: And We chose them (the Children of Israel) above the 'Alamin (mankind, and jinns) [during the time of Musa (Moses)] with knowledge,
32.arberry: and We chose them, out of a knowledge, above all beings,

33.sahih_international: And We gave them of signs that in which there was a clear trial.
33.pickthall: And We gave them portents wherein was a clear trial.
33.yusuf_ali: And granted them Signs in which there was a manifest trial
33.shakir: And We gave them of the communications wherein was clear blessing.
33.muhammad_sarwar: and sent them revelations of which some were a clear trial for them.
33.mohsin_khan: And granted them signs in which there was a plain trial.
33.arberry: and gave them signs wherein there was a manifest trial.

34.yusuf_ali: As to these (Quraish), they say forsooth:

35.sahih_international: "There is not but our first death, and we will not be resurrected.
35.pickthall: There is naught but our first death, and we shall not be raised again.
35.yusuf_ali: "There is nothing beyond our first death, and we shall not be raised again.
35.shakir: There is naught but our first death and we shall not be raised again.
35.muhammad_sarwar: "After we die, we shall never be raised to life again.
35.mohsin_khan: "There is nothing but our first death, and we shall not be resurrected.
35.arberry: 'There is nothing but our first death; we shall not be revived.

36.sahih_international: Then bring [back] our forefathers, if you should be truthful."
36.pickthall: Bring back our fathers, if ye speak the truth!
36.yusuf_ali: "Then bring (back) our forefathers, if what ye say is true!"
36.shakir: So bring our fathers (back), if you are truthful.
36.muhammad_sarwar: Bring back to life our fathers if what you say is true".
36.mohsin_khan: "Then bring back our fore-fathers, if you speak the truth!"
36.arberry: Bring us our fathers, if you speak truly!'

37.sahih_international: Are they better or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them, [for] indeed, they were criminals.
37.pickthall: Are they better, or the folk of Tubb'a and those before them? We destroyed them, for surely they were guilty.
37.yusuf_ali: What! Are they better than the people of Tubba and those who were before them? We destroyed them because they were guilty of sin.
37.shakir: Are they better or the people of Tubba and those before them? We destroyed them, for surely they were guilty.
37.muhammad_sarwar: Are they better than the tribe of Tubba (name of a Yemenite tribal chief) and those who lived before them? We destroyed them. They were criminals.
37.mohsin_khan: Are they better or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them because they were indeed Mujrimun (disbelievers, polytheists, sinners, criminals, etc.).
37.arberry: Are they better, or the people of Tubba' and those before them whom We destroyed? They were surely sinners.

38.sahih_international: And We did not create the heavens and earth and that between them in play.
38.pickthall: And We created not the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in play.
38.yusuf_ali: We created not the heavens, the earth, and all between them, merely in (idle) sport:
38.shakir: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in sport.
38.muhammad_sarwar: We have not created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them for Our own amusement.
38.mohsin_khan: And We created not the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, for mere play,
38.arberry: We created not the heavens and earth, and all that between them is, in play;

39.sahih_international: We did not create them except in truth, but most of them do not know.
39.pickthall: We created them not save with truth; but most of them know not.
39.yusuf_ali: We created them not except for just ends: but most of them do not understand.
39.shakir: We did not create them both but with the truth, but most of them do not know.
39.muhammad_sarwar: We have created them for a genuine purpose, but most people do not know.
39.mohsin_khan: We created them not except with truth (i.e. to examine and test those who are obedient and those who are disobedient and then reward the obedient ones and punish the disobedient ones), but most of them know not.
39.arberry: We created them not save in truth; but most of them know it not.

40.sahih_international: Indeed, the Day of Judgement is the appointed time for them all -
40.pickthall: Assuredly the Day of Decision is the term for all of them,
40.yusuf_ali: Verily the Day of sorting out is the time appointed for all of them,-
40.shakir: Surely the day of separation is their appointed term, of all of them
40.muhammad_sarwar: The appointed time for all of them will be the Day of Judgment
40.mohsin_khan: Verily, the Day of Judgement (when Allah will judge between the creatures) is the time appointed for all of them,
40.arberry: Surely the Day of Decision shall be their appointed time, all together,

41.sahih_international: The Day when no relation will avail a relation at all, nor will they be helped -
41.pickthall: A day when friend can in naught avail friend, nor can they be helped,
41.yusuf_ali: The Day when no protector can avail his client in aught, and no help can they receive,
41.shakir: The day on which a friend shall not avail (his) friend aught, nor shall they be helped,
41.muhammad_sarwar: (when wrong will be distinguished from right). On this day friends will be of no benefit to one another, nor will they receive any help
41.mohsin_khan: The Day when Maulan (a near relative) cannot avail Maulan (a near relative) in aught, and no help can they receive,
41.arberry: the day a master shall avail nothing a client, and they shall not be helped,

42.sahih_international: Except those [believers] on whom Allah has mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
42.pickthall: Save him on whom Allah hath mercy. Lo! He is the Mighty, the Merciful.
42.yusuf_ali: Except such as receive Allah's Mercy: for He is Exalted in Might, Most Merciful.
42.shakir: Save those on whom Allah shall have mercy; surely He is the Mighty the Merciful.
42.muhammad_sarwar: except for those to whom God grants mercy. He is Majestic and All-merciful.
42.mohsin_khan: Except him on whom Allah has Mercy. Verily, He is the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful.
42.arberry: save him upon whom God has mercy; He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.

43.shakir: Surely the tree of the Zaqqum,

44.yusuf_ali: Will be the food of the Sinful,-
44.shakir: Is the food of the sinful
44.mohsin_khan: Will be the food of the sinners,
44.arberry: is the food of the guilty,

45.sahih_international: Like murky oil, it boils within bellies
45.pickthall: Like molten brass, it seetheth in their bellies
45.yusuf_ali: Like molten brass; it will boil in their insides.
45.shakir: Like dregs of oil; it shall boil in (their) bellies,
45.muhammad_sarwar: It will be like molted brass which will boil in the bellies
45.mohsin_khan: Like boiling oil, it will boil in the bellies,
45.arberry: like molten copper, bubbling in the belly

46.sahih_international: Like the boiling of scalding water.
46.pickthall: As the seething of boiling water.
46.yusuf_ali: Like the boiling of scalding water.
46.shakir: Like the boiling of hot water.
46.mohsin_khan: Like the boiling of scalding water.

47.sahih_international: [It will be commanded], "Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire,
47.pickthall: (And it will be said): Take him and drag him to the midst of hell,
47.yusuf_ali: (A voice will cry: "Seize ye him and drag him into the midst of the Blazing Fire!
47.shakir: Seize him, then drag him down into the middle of the hell;
47.muhammad_sarwar: (It will be said of such sinners), "Seize them and drag them into the middle of hell.
47.mohsin_khan: (It will be said) "Seize him and drag him into the midst of blazing Fire,
47.arberry: 'Take him, and thrust him into the midst of Hell,

48.sahih_international: Then pour over his head from the torment of scalding water."
48.pickthall: Then pour upon his head the torment of boiling water.
48.yusuf_ali: "Then pour over his head the Penalty of Boiling Water,
48.shakir: Then pour above his head of the torment of the boiling water:
48.muhammad_sarwar: Then pour unto their heads the boiling water to torment them".
48.mohsin_khan: "Then pour over his head the torment of boiling water,
48.arberry: then pour over his head the chastisement of boiling water!'

49.sahih_international: [It will be said], "Taste! Indeed, you are the honored, the noble!
49.pickthall: (Saying): Taste! Lo! thou wast forsooth the mighty, the noble!
49.yusuf_ali: "Taste thou (this)! Truly wast thou mighty, full of honour!
49.shakir: Taste; you forsooth are the mighty, the honorable:
49.muhammad_sarwar: They will be told, "Suffer the torment. You had thought yourselves to be majestic and honorable.
49.mohsin_khan: "Taste you (this)! Verily, you were (pretending to be) the mighty, the generous!
49.arberry: 'Taste! Surely thou art the mighty, the noble.

50.sahih_international: Indeed, this is what you used to dispute."
50.pickthall: Lo! this is that whereof ye used to doubt.
50.yusuf_ali: "Truly this is what ye used to doubt!"
50.shakir: Surely this is what you disputed about.
50.muhammad_sarwar: This is the torment that you persistently doubted".
50.mohsin_khan: "Verily! This is that whereof you used to doubt!"
50.arberry: This is that concerning which you were doubting.'

51.sahih_international: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place;
51.pickthall: Lo! those who kept their duty will be in a place secured.
51.yusuf_ali: As to the Righteous (they will be) in a position of Security,
51.shakir: Surely those who guard (against evil) are in a secure place,
51.muhammad_sarwar: The pious ones will be in a secure place
51.mohsin_khan: Verily! The Muttaqun (pious - see V. 2:2), will be in place of Security (Paradise).
51.arberry: Surely the godfearing shall be in a station secure

53.sahih_international: Wearing [garments of] fine silk and brocade, facing each other.
53.pickthall: Attired in silk and silk embroidery, facing one another.
53.yusuf_ali: Dressed in fine silk and in rich brocade, they will face each other;
53.shakir: They shall wear of fine and thick silk, (sitting) face to face;
53.muhammad_sarwar: clothed in fine silk and rich brocade, sitting face to face with one another.
53.mohsin_khan: Dressed in fine silk and (also) in thick silk, facing each other,
53.arberry: robed in silk and brocade, set face to face.

54.sahih_international: Thus. And We will marry them to fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes.
54.pickthall: Even so (it will be). And We shall wed them unto fair ones with wide, lovely eyes.
54.yusuf_ali: So; and We shall join them to fair women with beautiful, big, and lustrous eyes.
54.shakir: Thus (shall it be), and We will wed them with Houris pure, beautiful ones.
54.muhammad_sarwar: We shall unite them to maidens with big black and white lovely eyes.
54.mohsin_khan: So (it will be), and We shall marry them to Houris (female fair ones) with wide, lovely eyes.
54.arberry: Even so; and We shall espouse them to wide-eyed houris,

55.sahih_international: They will call therein for every [kind of] fruit - safe and secure.
55.pickthall: They call therein for every fruit in safety.
55.yusuf_ali: There can they call for every kind of fruit in peace and security;
55.shakir: They shall call therein for every fruit in security;
55.muhammad_sarwar: They will be offered all kinds of fruits, in peace and security.
55.mohsin_khan: They will call therein for every kind of fruit in peace and security;
55.arberry: therein calling for every fruit, secure.

56.sahih_international: They will not taste death therein except the first death, and He will have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire
56.pickthall: They taste not death therein, save the first death. And He hath saved them from the doom of hell,
56.yusuf_ali: Nor will they there taste Death, except the first death; and He will preserve them from the Penalty of the Blazing Fire,-
56.shakir: They shall not taste therein death except the first death, and He will save them from the punishment of the hell,
56.muhammad_sarwar: They will not experience any death other than that which they have already been through.
56.mohsin_khan: They will never taste death therein except the first death (of this world), and He will save them from the torment of the blazing Fire,
56.arberry: They shall not taste therein of death, save the first death, And He shall guard them against the chastisement of Hell --

57.sahih_international: As bounty from your Lord. That is what is the great attainment.
57.pickthall: A bounty from thy Lord. That is the supreme triumph.
57.yusuf_ali: As a Bounty from thy Lord! that will be the supreme achievement!
57.shakir: A grace from your Lord; this is the great achievement.
57.muhammad_sarwar: God will protect them from the torment of hell as a favor from your Lord. (Muhammad), this is certainly the greatest triumph.
57.mohsin_khan: As a Bounty from your Lord! That will be the supreme success!
57.arberry: a bounty from thy Lord; that is the mighty triumph.

58.sahih_international: And indeed, We have eased the Qur'an in your tongue that they might be reminded.
58.pickthall: And We have made (this Scripture) easy in thy language only that they may heed.
58.yusuf_ali: Verily, We have made this (Qur'an) easy, in thy tongue, in order that they may give heed.
58.shakir: So have We made it easy in your tongue that they may be mindful.
58.muhammad_sarwar: We have made the Quran easy for you to recite so that perhaps they may take heed.
58.mohsin_khan: Certainly, We have made this (Quran) easy in your tongue, in order that they may remember.
58.arberry: Now We have made it easy by thy tongue, that haply they may remember.

59.sahih_international: So watch, [O Muhammad]; indeed, they are watching [for your end].
59.pickthall: Wait then (O Muhammad). Lo! they (too) are waiting.
59.yusuf_ali: So wait thou and watch; for they (too) are waiting.
59.shakir: Therefore wait; surely they are waiting.
59.muhammad_sarwar: Wait (for God's decree) and they too will be waiting.
59.mohsin_khan: Wait then (O Muhammad SAW); Verily, they (too) are waiting.
59.arberry: So be on the watch; they too are on the watch.
